stages.name: Foundations
stages.title: Company-level foundations
stages.note: Organisational requirements that must be in place before any product-specific work begins.

items.title: Documented Security Development Lifecycle
items.description: Maintain a documented SDL defining phases, roles and responsibilities. External certification (IEC 62443-4-1, ISO/IEC 27001) is optional but creates a presumption of conformity.
items.inference_criteria: Verify if the project documents a secure development lifecycle (SDL) or guidelines covering security review, testing, and contribution policies.
items.interview_prompt: Do you have a documented Security Development Lifecycle (SDL) or security practices that your engineering team follows?

items.title: Evidence of conformity with the SDL
items.description: Where no external certification is held, keep documented evidence of internal conformity with the SDL.
items.inference_criteria: Verify documented internal audit or checklist evidence confirming the development team follows the SDL.
items.interview_prompt: Do you maintain internal evidence/checklists demonstrating your team follows your secure development process?

items.title: SDL covers secure-by-design and secure-by-default
items.description: The SDL must explicitly address how the product minimises its attack surface without configuration by the end user.
items.inference_criteria: Verify if documentation explains how the product is secure by default (e.g., minimal open ports, least privilege, safe default settings).
items.interview_prompt: Is your software designed and configured to be secure-by-default out of the box without requiring manual security hardening by the user?

items.title: EU Authorised Representative (non-EU manufacturers)
items.description: Manufacturers outside the EU must designate, by written mandate, a representative established in the EU, named in the technical documentation and the DoC.
items.inference_criteria: Verify if a written mandate appointing an EU Authorised Representative is declared, or if the manufacturer is established in the EU (making this N/A).
items.interview_prompt: If your company is based outside the EU, have you appointed an EU Authorised Representative with a written mandate (or are you established in the EU)?

stages.name: Before development
stages.title: Before development begins
stages.note: Classification, risk assessment and technical prerequisites set the scope for everything that follows.

items.title: Determine product classification
items.description: Identify whether the product is Default, Important Class I/II or Critical (Annexes III & IV). Classification determines the conformity assessment route.
items.inference_criteria: Verify if the product classification is documented (Default / Class I / Class II / Critical) according to CRA Annexes III & IV.
items.interview_prompt: Have you verified whether your product qualifies as a standard Default digital product under CRA (vs. Important Class I/II or Critical)?

items.title: Identify the conformity assessment route
items.description: Default: Module A self-assessment. Important Class I: Module A with a harmonised standard, else B+C or H. Important Class II & Critical: always via a Notified Body. Lead times of 4–10 months are common.
items.inference_criteria: Verify if the conformity assessment route is identified (Module A internal control for Default products vs. third-party certification).
items.interview_prompt: Is your conformity assessment route confirmed as Module A (internal control self-assessment)?

items.title: Product-specific cybersecurity risk assessment
items.description: Perform a risk assessment before development. Retain all versions; the initial pre-development version is part of the technical documentation.
items.inference_criteria: Verify if a product-specific cybersecurity risk assessment is recorded covering intended use and foreseeable misuse.
items.interview_prompt: Have you performed and documented a cybersecurity risk assessment for this product?

items.title: Threat modelling
items.description: Identify attack surface, threat actors, attack vectors and resulting security requirements. Document the methodology used.
items.inference_criteria: Verify if threat modelling documentation exists outlining entry points, trust boundaries, and mitigations.
items.interview_prompt: Does the engineering team maintain a documented threat model for the application architecture?

items.title: Third-party & open-source component policy
items.description: Define how third-party and open-source components are selected, evaluated and approved, including minimum EOL and vulnerability-response obligations.
items.inference_criteria: Verify whether guidelines exist for evaluating third-party and open-source dependencies for security and license risks before adoption.
items.interview_prompt: Do you follow a documented policy for screening and approving third-party libraries and dependencies before adding them?

items.title: EOL check for tools and dependencies
items.description: Check the End-of-Life date of all key tools, kernels, databases and libraries. Avoid components whose EOL falls within the product's support lifetime.
items.inference_criteria: Deterministic check: automated dependency EOL and vulnerability screening tool configuration.
items.interview_prompt: Do you run automated tools (Dependabot, Renovate, Snyk) to monitor dependencies and runtimes for end-of-life?

items.title: Storage encryption feasibility
items.description: Confirm the target hardware/runtime supports encryption of data at rest; a mandatory requirement that may force architectural adjustments.
items.inference_criteria: Verify documentation assessing storage encryption feasibility for data at rest and data in transit.
items.interview_prompt: Is sensitive user data encrypted at rest and in transit, with encryption feasibility documented?

items.title: Minimal attack-surface design
items.description: Plan to remove or disable by default every interface, service, port and protocol not required for the intended function.
items.inference_criteria: Deterministic check: container least privilege (non-root USER), minimal base images, and absence of development debug servers in production.
items.interview_prompt: Are production containers and services configured with minimal attack surface (non-root user, unused ports closed)?

items.title: Default credential policy
items.description: Ship with no default passwords, or force the user to set a unique credential on first use.
items.inference_criteria: Verify that no default or hardcoded passwords exist; initial secrets must be generated or set by the user upon initialization.
items.interview_prompt: Does your application strictly prohibit hardcoded default credentials and require user-supplied passwords/tokens?

stages.name: During development
stages.title: During development
stages.note: Secure coding, testing and the update mechanism, evidenced throughout the build.

items.title: Cybersecurity-focused test plan
items.description: Test cases targeting authentication, access control, input validation, encryption and error handling. Documented and retained in the technical file.
items.inference_criteria: Deterministic check: automated CI test pipeline configured and passing on pull requests and pushes.
items.interview_prompt: Do you run automated security and functional tests on every pull request?

items.title: Evidence of SDL compliance
items.description: Demonstrate, with documented evidence, that the SDL was followed at each phase.
items.inference_criteria: Verify branch protection and mandatory peer code review before merging changes to release branches.
items.interview_prompt: Do you enforce mandatory peer code review and branch protection on your default branch?

items.title: Penetration testing / vulnerability assessment
items.description: Conduct security testing on the product or a representative build before release (DAST/SAST/Pen-test).
items.inference_criteria: Deterministic check: SAST, DAST, or secret scanning automated pipeline (CodeQL, Semgrep, Trivy, Gitleaks).
items.interview_prompt: Do you run automated code security scanners (CodeQL, SAST, secret detection) in CI?

items.title: Secure software update mechanism
items.description: An authenticated, integrity-verified update mechanism, verifiable by the device before installation and automatic where feasible.
items.inference_criteria: Deterministic check: automated, authenticated release workflow with cryptographic checksums or signatures.
items.interview_prompt: Are software releases built through an automated, authenticated release pipeline with signed checksums?

items.title: Data minimisation
items.description: Collect, process and store only the data strictly necessary for the intended function.
items.inference_criteria: Verify data minimisation statement ensuring only strictly necessary telemetry or user data is processed.
items.interview_prompt: Does your product enforce data minimisation, processing only personal or operational data strictly necessary for functionality?

stages.name: Before release
stages.title: Before product release
stages.note: SBOM, network audit, EOL, conformity assessment, CE marking and the technical file.

items.title: SBOM prepared and vulnerability-screened
items.description: Prepare an SBOM covering at least all top-level dependencies and verify no component carries a known, already-patched vulnerability. Including a resolved CVE is a direct violation.
items.inference_criteria: Deterministic check: SBOM generated automatically during build and screened for known CVEs.
items.interview_prompt: Do you generate an automated Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for every release and check it for known vulnerabilities?

items.title: SBOM in machine-readable format
items.description: Store the SBOM as SPDX or CycloneDX (JSON/XML). PDF may be rejected as non-machine-readable.
items.inference_criteria: Deterministic check: SBOM exported in standard machine-readable format (CycloneDX or SPDX JSON).
items.interview_prompt: Is your SBOM exported in an industry standard format (CycloneDX or SPDX JSON)?

items.title: Inbound connections list
items.description: List and individually justify every inbound connection and open port; remove or disable by default anything not required.
items.inference_criteria: Verify documentation listing all inbound network ports, listening services, and justification.
items.interview_prompt: Do you document all listening ports and incoming network connections required by your software?

items.title: Outbound connections list
items.description: Audit and justify all outbound connections, including those from the OS, third-party libraries and telemetry.
items.inference_criteria: Verify documentation listing all outbound network endpoints, telemetry destinations, and remote APIs contacted.
items.interview_prompt: Do you document all outbound endpoints, third-party APIs, and external servers contacted by your application?

items.title: Declare the product End-of-Life
items.description: Calculate and declare the EOL; it cannot exceed the EOL of key dependencies. Minimum 5-year support period unless the expected use lifetime is shorter.
items.inference_criteria: Verify explicit declaration of support period / End-of-Life date (at least 5 years unless product expected lifetime is shorter).
items.interview_prompt: Have you published a declared End-of-Life (EOL) support date guaranteeing at least 5 years of security updates?

items.title: Complete the conformity assessment
items.description: Carry out the applicable procedure (Module A, or B+C / H / Notified Body) and document it before affixing CE marking.
items.inference_criteria: Verify record of completed conformity assessment procedure (Module A verification).
items.interview_prompt: Have you completed and signed off on your internal conformity assessment record?

items.title: Prepare the EU Declaration of Conformity
items.description: Draft and sign the DoC per Annex V, referencing the regulation, product and assessment procedure. Keep available for 10 years.
items.inference_criteria: Verify formal EU Declaration of Conformity drafted containing CRA Annex V required elements.
items.interview_prompt: Has your company drafted and approved an EU Declaration of Conformity (DoC)?

items.title: Affix the CE marking
items.description: Apply visible, legible, indelible CE marking. No CE marking, no EU market from 11 Dec 2027.
items.inference_criteria: Verify documentation explaining how the CE marking will be affixed (on product packaging, label, website, or accompanying docs).
items.interview_prompt: Do you have a defined plan for affixing or displaying the CE marking on product packaging or accompanying documentation?

items.title: Compile the technical file
items.description: Assemble the Annex VII package: description, risk assessment, SDL evidence, test results, SBOM, connection audits, DoC and EOL declaration.
items.inference_criteria: Verify compilation of Annex VII technical documentation file.
items.interview_prompt: Is your Annex VII technical documentation file assembled and ready for potential market surveillance inspection?

items.title: 10-year retention plan
items.description: Archive all technical documentation, including every SBOM version, for at least 10 years from first market placement.
items.inference_criteria: Verify explicit 10-year retention commitment for the technical file and Declaration of Conformity.
items.interview_prompt: Does your company have a data archive procedure to preserve technical compliance files for 10 years?

items.title: User-facing documentation
items.description: Communicate intended use, cybersecurity properties, how to configure security, the declared EOL and how to report vulnerabilities.
items.inference_criteria: Verify user-facing instructions detailing secure installation, configuration, and update procedures.
items.interview_prompt: Do your user-facing docs (README or manuals) provide clear instructions on secure installation and security updates?

items.title: Vulnerability disclosure contact published
items.description: Publish a single, actively monitored point of contact for reporting vulnerabilities.
items.inference_criteria: Verify presence of a single contact point (email address or private vulnerability reporting) for reporting security vulnerabilities.
items.interview_prompt: Do you provide a public security contact email (e.g. security@yourcompany.com) or vulnerability disclosure channel?

stages.name: After release
stages.title: After product release
stages.note: Ongoing monitoring, the Article 14 reporting timeline and update obligations across the support period.

items.title: Update risk assessment on significant change
items.description: Reassess when a major product change, significant new threat or exploited vulnerability is identified; document the trigger and outcome.
items.inference_criteria: Verify policy triggering cybersecurity risk re-assessment when substantial product modifications occur.
items.interview_prompt: Do you have a policy to re-evaluate product cybersecurity risks whenever major architectural changes are made?

items.title: Automated SBOM vulnerability monitoring
items.description: Deploy tooling that monitors SBOM components against live feeds (NVD, EUVD, OSV) frequently enough to meet the 24-hour reporting window. Manual monitoring is insufficient.
items.inference_criteria: Deterministic check: continuous scheduled vulnerability scanning against live CVE databases (OSV, NVD).
items.interview_prompt: Do you continuously screen your dependency SBOM against active vulnerability feeds on a schedule?

items.title: 24-hour initial vulnerability report
items.description: On becoming aware of an actively exploited vulnerability, file an initial report within 24 hours via ENISA's single reporting platform. Applies from 11 Sep 2026.
items.inference_criteria: Verify explicit 24-hour notification protocol for actively exploited vulnerabilities to CSIRTs/ENISA (Art. 14(2)).
items.interview_prompt: Does your incident response plan include notifying national CSIRTs/ENISA within 24 hours of an actively exploited zero-day?

items.title: 72-hour technical report
items.description: Submit a detailed technical report to ENISA and the national CSIRT within 72 hours, including severity and any mitigation.
items.inference_criteria: Verify 72-hour technical assessment report protocol (Art. 14(3)).
items.interview_prompt: Does your incident procedure commit to delivering a detailed technical assessment to authorities within 72 hours?

items.title: Final report within 14 days of remediation
items.description: Submit a final report no later than 14 days after a security update or workaround is made available.
items.inference_criteria: Verify final report delivery within 14 days of remediation patch or 1 month of incident resolution (Art. 14(4)).
items.interview_prompt: Do you have a protocol to submit a final incident/vulnerability closure report once a fix is deployed?

items.title: Severe incident reporting
items.description: Report severe incidents affecting product security on the same 24/72-hour timeline.
items.inference_criteria: Verify severe cybersecurity incident notification protocol.
items.interview_prompt: Does your security procedure cover rapid reporting of severe security incidents impacting the product availability or user data?

items.title: Automatic update for third-party vulnerabilities
items.description: Maintain an automatic update system able to patch third-party component vulnerabilities. A fix within 24 hours exempts reporting, not fixing.
items.inference_criteria: Deterministic check: automated patching workflow for vulnerable third-party components.
items.interview_prompt: Do you use automated pull requests (Dependabot/Renovate) to quickly test and deploy third-party security patches?

items.title: Security updates free of charge
items.description: Provide all security updates free of charge for the duration of the support period.
items.inference_criteria: Verify formal commitment that all security patches will be provided free of charge throughout the support lifetime.
items.interview_prompt: Do you commit to providing all security patches free of charge to customers throughout the product support period?

items.title: Advance notice of End-of-Life
items.description: Notify users at least 12 months before the final security update, where feasible.
items.inference_criteria: Verify policy to notify users in advance before product support reaches End-of-Life.
items.interview_prompt: Do you commit to notifying customers well in advance before product security support ends?

items.title: Corrective measures for non-compliant products
items.description: Remediate, withdraw or recall non-compliant products and notify market surveillance. Inaction is itself a violation.
items.inference_criteria: Verify corrective action and potential recall procedure for non-compliant products placed on the EU market.
items.interview_prompt: Do you have a documented process to issue corrective updates or product notices if non-compliance is identified?
